paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
model_annotation: This chart is a nested donut (ring) chart consisting of two concentric rings that represent two different measures of ambiguity: "Ambiguity Std" on the outer ring and "Max Ambiguity" on the inner ring. The outer ring is divided into four slices corresponding to different standard deviation values: "Std: 0.0" shown in a very dark navy/teal color at approximately 49.0%, "Std: 0.47" in a dark blue at approximately 47.7%, "Std: 0.82" in a medium dark teal-blue at approximately 7.0% (a narrow slice at the top), and "Std: 0.94" in a medium blue at approximately 5.0% (also a narrow slice). The inner ring is divided into three slices representing maximum ambiguity values: "Max: 1" in a medium cyan-blue at approximately 39.0%, "Max: 2" in a lighter sky blue at approximately 38.0%, and "Max: 3" in a very light, nearly pale blue at approximately 14.2%. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or adjacent to each slice. Two separate legends are provided to the right of the chart, one for each ring, clearly distinguishing the color coding for the outer "Ambiguity Std" categories and the inner "Max Ambiguity" categories. In the outer ring, the two largest slices (Std: 0.0 and Std: 0.47) dominate and are nearly equal in size, while the two smaller slices are considerably narrower. In the inner ring, the Max: 1 and Max: 2 slices are roughly similar in proportion, with Max: 3 being noticeably smaller. No slices appear to be visually exploded or offset from the rings.
